more_info.overview: Ethoxylated mono- and diglycerides are glyceride preparations further reacted with ethylene oxide. The US specification principally uses stearic, palmitic and myristic fatty-acid starting materials. The resulting ingredient has emulsifying and dough-conditioning functions. FDA lists applications in yeast-raised bakery products, cakes, icings, whipped vegetable-oil toppings, frozen desserts and certain coffee creamers, with separate use limits. The fatty-acid source is not fixed as exclusively animal or plant by the chemical name.
more_info.origin: Manufactured from edible fats or fatty acids and glycerol, followed by reaction with ethylene oxide. The regulation does not specify the fatty acids as exclusively plant or animal derived.
more_info.uses: Specified US uses include bakery pan-release preparations, yeast-raised bakery products, cakes, whipped vegetable-oil toppings, icings, frozen desserts and certain milk or cream substitutes for coffee. Each application has its own maximum.
more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use follows the preparation-specific conditions in 21 CFR 172.834, checked in 2026.
